judgments.basis: SEC Staff Accounting Bulletin No. 122 (rescinding SAB 121, effective for periods beginning after 2024-12-15); ASC 450-20-25-2 (recognition only when a loss is probable and estimable); custody agreement clauses 2.1, 2.2, 3.1; proof of control and sub-custodian statement.
judgments.proposedConclusion: Yes, DemoCo is obligated to return the assets or their value (clause 3.1) and remains obligated for the ETH placed with the sub-custodian (clause 2.2), so it safeguards both populations. Under SAB 122, which rescinded SAB 121's requirement to recognize a safeguarding liability and corresponding asset, holding the assets is not itself a liability: DemoCo applies ASC 450-20 to the risk of loss from safeguarding and discloses the nature and amount of the assets safeguarded, the controls and the risks. The customer assets are not DemoCo's assets and are not recognized.

alternatives.notes: Rejected: recovery attempts have failed and the make-whole obligation is contractual; disclosure alone would understate liabilities.

judgments.basis: ASC 450-20-25-2 (probable and estimable); ASC 450-20-30-1 (best estimate within the range — the ETH lost is known, only its price moves); ASC 450-20-50-1; incident report; clause 7.2.
judgments.proposedConclusion: Yes. Recovery has failed and clause 7.2 obliges DemoCo to make the affected customers whole, so a loss is probable; it is estimable at the 10 ETH lost measured at the 2026-06-30 price of 2,250 USD, 22,500 USD, with no insurance recovery asserted. The accrual is recorded as a safeguarding loss against a liability to the customers, remeasured each period until settled in ETH or its value.

judgments.basis: ASC 450-20-25-2 and 450-20-50-3 to 50-5 (disclosure of reasonably possible losses); SAB 122 disclosure expectations; proof of control; sub-custodian statement.
judgments.proposedConclusion: No loss is probable: the BTC keys are in DemoCo HSMs with a verified proof of control and the ETH sits segregated with the sub-custodian; no incident affects these populations. A loss is at most reasonably possible given the inherent risks of key custody, so no accrual is recorded and the risk is disclosed with the safeguarded amounts.
